newsitem.title: USA: Sun to quit API at end of '96 to cut costs.
newsitem.headline: Sun to quit API at end of '96 to cut costs.

text.p: Sun Co Inc said it was quitting its membership in the American Petroleum Institute (API) at the end of 1996 as part of its continuing efforts to cut costs, and to better compete with other independent refiners.
An API official declined to disclose the amount of Sun's annual membership dues, but added that the trade group plans to release a statement on Sun's withdrawal later Tuesday.
"Our withdrawal is a logical step for Sun, and it involves no negative feelings toward the API," Sun's Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Robert Campbell said in a statement.
"To the contrary, API has consistently been helpful over the years in many aspects of our business and we have enjoyed our long associations with the organization," Campbell said.
An industry source who declined to be identified said he thought Sun was likely paying about $1 million a year to keep its API membership.
He said API dues are calculated using a complex formula under which bigger companies pay more than smaller ones.
"Sun is one of the compamies who have complained about the formula," the source said.
A spokeswoman at Sun had no comment on the annual dues or Sun's alleged objection to the formula, but did note that Sun is the last of its independent competitors to quit API.

"There are no independents who just do refining and marketing who are in API," said said Shannon Breuer, manager of communications at Sun. "Why should we absorb that cost when no one else does?" Breuer asked.
Among independents no longer in the trade group, Breuer included Tosco Corp, Crown Central Petroleum Corp as well as Ultramar Corp and Diamond Shamrock Inc, which recently announced plans to merge.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
